# Ensure every Main Street card has a dedicated 64×64 sprite

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (24) — new staff art.** Per-role sprites (or a documented shared
   set), produced by the producer.
4. **Events (36) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; duplicate an existing representative
   where one fits, otherwise produce a new category sprite.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 24 | New per-role (or shared) source art | 24 |
| Event | 36 | `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | up to 12 |
| **Total newly produced** | | | **up to 45** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. Using a category representative for cards it was
not drawn for (e.g. Tax Audit art for `Rainy Day`) is semantically loose — the
producer may prefer a bespoke category sprite for all 12.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision:** `Florist` (business + staff) and
  `Community Garden` (community-space + event) share a name, so name-keyed
  resolution gives both the same sprite. Accepted and documented; assert in
  the drift guard rather than re-key by family (the public API stays name-based).
- **Category-art fidelity:** reusing an existing event sprite for a different
  event (e.g. Tax Audit art for `Rainy Day`) is visually loose; the producer
  may choose bespoke category sprites for all 12.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).

## Problem

`rasteriseSvgToTexture()` in `src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts` hard-codes a 4x oversampling factor:

```ts
const qualityScale = Math.max(4, dpr);
const targetW = Math.round(width * qualityScale);
```

Every card SVG is therefore rasterised at 4x its logical size (a 140x80 card becomes a 560x320 canvas) regardless of how large it is actually drawn. Consequences:

- The 64x64 art zone within that SVG occupies 256x256 device pixels, forcing the embedded bitmap to be upscaled 4x (see CG-0MUCM36EQ008YP4R for the complementary embedded-art fix).
- ~16x more texture memory and GPU upload bandwidth than the display actually needs.
- Texture cache keys encode the logical size + DPR, not the rendered size, so every card is over-allocated.

## Proposed change

Rasterise at the display native resolution: `qualityScale = dpr` (i.e. render at `width x dpr`), so textures are allocated at exactly the device pixels they occupy. Retain a small supersample (e.g. 1x) for the vector stroke/text quality if visual review shows artefacts.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `rasteriseSvgToTexture()` no longer hard-codes a 4x multiplier; the render resolution is derived from the display density (DPR)
2. Existing `SvgHelpers` unit/browser tests are updated to assert the new resolution contract
3. Card textures are allocated at `width * dpr` (verified by a test asserting canvas dimensions)
4. No visual regression in card text/vector stroke legibility (reviewed at DPR 1, 2 and 3)
5. Unit tests pass (`npm test -- --project unit`)
6. Build succeeds (`npm run build`)

## Interaction with CG-0MUCM36EQ008YP4R

The two fixes are complementary. Reducing the SVG rasterisation to native resolution lowers the required embedded-art resolution; raising the embedded art makes the card crisp at any rasterisation scale. Decide the final art resolution (64x64, 128x128 or 256x256) once this change lands.

## Open question (producer review)

Interpretation of "native resolution" in the request is ambiguous. This work item assumes it means "the display native resolution (DPR-matched)" rather than the 4x quality scale. If instead it means "generate the card SVG canvas at a higher intrinsic size (e.g. 560x320 native with a 256x256 art zone)", the ACs above should be rewritten. Confirm before implementing.

## Summary

Add a hover tooltip to the persistent synergy lines drawn between adjacent
synergistic businesses on the Main Street board. Hovering a line explains the
shared synergy type and the per-turn effect that link has on each of the two
connected cards.

## User Story

As a Main Street player, I want to hover over a synergy line and see what that
synergy does — the shared type and the coins/reputation each linked business
gains from it — so that I can understand *why* two businesses are connected and
plan my street deliberately, instead of guessing from the line colour alone.

## Problem Statement

The board draws coloured synergy lines between adjacent businesses that share a
synergy type, but the lines are purely decorative: hovering them does nothing.
The player sees that two cards are linked but not which synergy type they share,
the rate that applies, or the value of that specific connection. The only
synergy information available today is the per-card `Synergy: <types>` line in
the business-slot tooltip, which does not explain the link or its magnitude.

## Existing State

- `drawSynergyLines()` in
  `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` draws a
  two-pass `Phaser.GameObjects.Graphics` line (core + glow) per synergy pair and
  adds it to `streetContainer`. The graphics objects are **not interactive** —
  there is no input handler on them.
- `computeSynergyPairs()` in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyNeighbors.ts`
  returns `SynergyPair { fromIndex, toIndex, sharedSynergy }`, the data the
  renderer iterates to draw each line. Sold cards still participate as pair
  endpoints (CG-0MT5XUE2200047IJ).
- Per-card synergy maths lives in
  `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`:
  `computeSynergyBonus()` (coin), `computeSynergyRepBonus()` (reputation),
  `effectiveSynergyCoinBonus()` / `effectiveSynergyRepBonus()`. The difficulty
  multiplier is `config.synergyBonusPerNeighbor`.
- Existing formatting helpers live in
  `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` (`effectiveSynergyRate()`,
  `formatSynergyRate()`, `formatPerTurnReputation()`, `formatCurrency()`).
- Business-slot tooltips already use the shared `TooltipManager`
  (`s.tooltipManager?.show(info, x, y)` / `.hide()`); the manager is created
  only when `!s.replayMode`
  (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`) and already honours the
  `settingsPanel.showTooltips` toggle.

## Desired Change

1. Add a pure, unit-testable content builder — e.g.
   `buildSynergyLinkTooltipInfo(grid, fromIndex, toIndex, sharedSynergy, config, soldSlots?, gridDims?)`
   in `MainStreetFormatting.ts` — that returns the tooltip text for one link.
2. In `drawSynergyLines()`, give each line a **narrow, invisible interactive hit
   area** (parented into `streetContainer`, drawn/recreated with the rest of the
   street layer) wired to `tooltipManager.show(...)` on `pointerover` and
   `tooltipManager.hide()` on `pointerout`.
3. Guard the wiring the same way existing slot tooltips are: no tooltip in
   `replayMode` and no tooltip when `tooltipManager` is absent; the
   `showTooltips` setting continues to be enforced by `TooltipManager` itself.
4. Ensure the hit area does not swallow the existing business-slot hover/click
   interactions except immediately along the line (see Constraints).

### Suggested tooltip format (implementation may refine wording)

```
Food synergy
Bakery  ⟷  Diner
Bakery: +2 coins/turn from this link
Diner: +1 coins/turn from this link
+5 reputation/turn  (only when a reputation-synergy contribution exists)
```

Sold endpoints are called out explicitly, e.g.
`Bakery (sold): earns nothing, but still anchors this synergy`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Hovering a persistent synergy line shows a tooltip that names the shared
  synergy type and states the per-turn coin and/or reputation effect of that
  link for **each** endpoint, computed with the active difficulty multiplier
  (`config.synergyBonusPerNeighbor`).
- The tooltip is hidden when the pointer leaves the line, and is not shown at
  all in replay mode; the existing `settingsPanel.showTooltips = false` toggle
  suppresses it (via `TooltipManager`).
- A sold endpoint is represented correctly: it earns nothing from the link
  itself, while the link still anchors synergy for the other endpoint, and the
  tooltip says so.
- The line hover hit area does not break the existing business-slot
  interactions: slot hover tooltips, click-to-place, sell, and upgrade
  targeting continue to work everywhere except the line's immediate vicinity.
- Unit tests cover the pure `buildSynergyLinkTooltipInfo()` builder (shared
  type, coin-only, reputation, sold endpoint, zero-synergy opt-out, difficulty
  multiplier) and an automated test covers the hover wiring on a rendered line.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Reuse the shared `TooltipManager` (`@ui`) — do **not** add a bespoke tooltip
  renderer, consistent with
  [Standardize TooltipManager across all games] (CG-0MPKE6W1C0047A44) and
  [Tooltip single-source fix] (CG-0MTJP6RNL008LGF3).
- Keep the content builder **pure** (no Phaser/scene dependency) so it can be
  unit-tested headless, mirroring `synergyLineEndpoints.ts`.
- Synergy lines are drawn **after** the slot rectangles in `drawSynergyLines()`,
  so their hit areas sit on top of the slot hit zones. The hit area must be
  narrow (a thin band around the segment, thick enough for a mouse but not so
  thick that it steals slot hover) and the chosen thickness/approach must be
  documented in a code comment.
- Hit areas are recreated on every `streetContainer` rebuild (the street layer
  is rebuilt by `refreshAll()`), so their creation must not leak listeners or
  leave stale objects behind.
- Reduced-motion: no animation is introduced; the tooltip appears/hides
  immediately, so reduced-motion preferences are unaffected.
- No new engine-level (`src/`) API is expected — Main Street-local formatting +
  renderer wiring only.
- Out of scope: tooltips on the transient synergy-formation animation line,
  changing the synergy formula, and changing line geometry/colours.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — Add an
  interactive hit area per synergy pair inside `drawSynergyLines()` and wire it
  to `s.tooltipManager`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — New pure
  `buildSynergyLinkTooltipInfo()` builder (shared synergy type + per-endpoint
  coin/reputation effect).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — Reuse/extract the
  per-link contribution maths if a per-neighbour share helper is needed
  (avoid duplicating the synergy formula).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyNeighbors.ts` — Source of
  `SynergyPair`; may need no change beyond typing.
- `tests/main-street/synergy-tooltip.test.ts` — New unit tests for the content
  builder.
- `tests/main-street/synergy-tooltip.browser.test.ts` — New browser test for
  hover wiring (or extend `tests/main-street/synergy-visuals.test.ts`).
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — Document the synergy-line tooltip
  interaction.
- `example-games/main-street/README.md` — Mention the tooltip in the synergy
  overview (if the README describes synergy lines).

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Assumption (documented, producer may adjust):** "the effect of that synergy"
  means the shared type plus the per-link per-turn coin/reputation contribution
  for each endpoint, rather than a generic rules paragraph. The suggested
  format above is a proposal; wording can change without altering the ACs.
- **Risk — per-link vs. card-total mismatch:** `computeSynergyBonus()` rounds
  the *total* across all matching neighbours, so a per-link share may not sum
  exactly to the displayed card total. The tooltip must not imply a precision
  it does not have; document the chosen presentation (per-link share formatted
  to at most one decimal, or card total) in the builder's doc comment.
- **Risk — input interception:** adding interactive objects on top of the slot
  hit zones can regress slot hover/click. Mitigation: narrow hit band + an
  explicit regression test for slot hover/click; keep the band culled with the
  line.
- **Risk — re-render churn:** `drawSynergyLines()` runs on every refresh; a
  fresh hit area per refresh must be destroyed with the container or it leaks.
- **Scope-creep guard:** any desire to also tooltip the *animated* formation
  line, restyle lines, or change synergy values must be filed as a separate
  work item, not folded into this one.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MM4REC2Z0GS2YKT** – Main Street: PRD Milestone 2 -- Full Content and Crafting/Building System (completed)
- **CG-0MQQHCJJ5009AB4X** – Fix Lighting Spike scene visibility (completed)
- **CG-0MQOBJ9BW006TTJR** – Main Street score tooltip should show calculation breakdown (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: effect, lines, provide, should, showing (+2 more)
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: effect, lines, provide, should, showing (+2 more)

## Failure Signature

- Test name: ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts — Last Round card: flips on the deck, settles at the resting position, and is omitted from its slot (waitForCondition timed out)
- Failing commit: latest `dev` at triage (root cause commit `21688987`, CG-0MUDMU0L8005YYE4)
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
Failure screenshot: tests/coloretto/__screenshots__/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts/... omits from slot-1.png. check tests/coloretto/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts:94:22 — Error: waitForCondition timed out. Seen during a full-suite run under heavy concurrent-agent CPU contention (load 25-49 on 16 cores); passes 26/26 in isolation at the same commit. discovered-from:CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA
```

## Root Cause

Not CPU-contention flakiness. The test now fails deterministically (~4 of 5 isolated runs at current `dev`).

Commit `21688987` (CG-0MUDMU0L8005YYE4) added `wholeRowValue()` and extended the Coloretto heuristic AI take gate to `netRowValue >= TAKE_THRESHOLD OR wholeRowValue >= TAKE_THRESHOLD` (`TAKE_THRESHOLD = 2`). A single bonus card has `wholeRowValue = BONUS_POINTS = 2`, so the AI now takes any row containing a bonus card.

In this test the AI's first turn may place a bonus card on a row (the session RNG defaults to `Math.random`, so the shuffled deck — and therefore the AI's first-turn card — varies run to run). After the human draws the Last Round card, the AI's final turn is then a TAKE, not a PLACE. The take animation (`playTakeAnimation`) uses flyers and never sets `flightCard`, so the test's fourth `waitForCondition` (`phase === 'animating' && flightCard !== null`) can never be satisfied; the round ends and phase becomes `round-scoring`.

Full investigation and evidence are recorded in the Plan-investigation comment.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout current `dev`: `git checkout <commit-hash>`
2. Run the failing test:
   `npx vitest run --project browser tests/coloretto/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts -t "Last Round card"`
3. Repeat several times: the failure depends on whether the AI's first turn drew a bonus card.

## Impact

Blocks the Coloretto browser suite on `dev`. The AI change is intended behaviour; the test's assumption that the AI's final turn is a placement is the brittle part.

## Recommended Fix Direction

Make the test deterministic or action-agnostic, e.g.:

- Control `scene.session.rows` before the human's placement so the AI has no row worth taking (forces a place, preserving the existing flight-card assertions); and/or
- Treat the AI's final turn as either place or take and wait on the round transition rather than `flightCard`.

## Key Files

- `tests/coloretto/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts`
- `example-games/coloretto/ColorettoAis.ts`
- `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoRenderer.ts`

1. The test `ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts — Last Round card: flips on the deck, settles at the resting position, and is omitted from its slot` passes reliably against the latest `dev` (e.g. 10 consecutive isolated runs, plus a normal suite run), with the AI's final turn either a place or a take.
2. The test no longer depends on the AI's strategy choice or on a specific shuffled deck (no new flakiness under CPU contention).
3. Documentation is updated only if the fix changes documented behaviour; a test-only fix requires no doc change.
4. The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Problem

`implement.py finish` removes the worktree and pushes the feature branch into `dev` **from the main checkout** (`repo_root`). The pre-push context-budget gate (`.githooks/pre-push`) measures the **working tree of the push source** — so when the commit being pushed changes `AGENTS.md`/thresholds, the main checkout is still at the old (breaching) dev state and the gate rejects the push, even though the pushed commit is compliant.

Observed while implementing CG-0MUFCL5N50023PHJ: `finish` passed build + full suite, committed `85ae7038`, then failed the push with `Context budget exceeded committed thresholds`. The commit had to be pushed manually from a worktree at the commit (`WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/dev`), where the gate measured the new files and passed without `CONTEXT_BUDGET_SKIP=1`.

## Impact

Any commit that legitimately changes the startup context surface (e.g. an `AGENTS.md` edit) cannot be pushed by `implement.py finish` without a bypass, undermining the gate and forcing manual recovery.

## Options

1. `finish` pushes from the worktree (new files present) before removing it, rather than from the main checkout.
2. The hook measures the **pushed commit** (e.g. `git show <local-sha>:AGENTS.md`) instead of the working tree.
3. `finish` fast-forwards the local parent branch to the commit before pushing.

Discovered during CG-0MUFCL5N50023PHJ; recovered manually.

The current `deploy.yml` workflow runs `npm run build`, which defaults to the `core-only` preset (Gym only). To deploy the full distribution with all games, the workflow must select the all-games preset via `GAMES_CONFIG`.

## Problem

The GitHub Pages deployment only publishes the Gym (core engine demo), not the full set of example games listed in `configs/full.json`.

## Solution

Update the "Build" step in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` to select the all-games preset:

```yaml
- name: Build
  run: GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run build
```

The config-driven game discovery plugin (`scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts`) reads `configs/full.json`, which lists all 8 games. Each game is resolved locally first (`example-games/<id>/...`) then as a sibling repo (`../tce-<id>/...`), so this works whether building from the launcher checkout or from a single-game repo.

> **Preset name corrected (plan, 2026-09-26):** this item originally referenced `GAMES_CONFIG=all` / `configs/all.json`. No such preset exists anywhere in the repository. `selectConfigPath()` treats an unknown preset name as a **hard error** (deliberately: it never silently falls back, because that would ship a distribution missing the requested games), so a literal implementation of the original wording would break the Pages build. The canonical "every game" preset is **`full`** (`configs/full.json`) — evidenced by `README.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md#config-driven-game-catalogue`, `configs/full.json`'s own `$comment`, CG-0MTRO77XA006YZZC AC5 (`full=all`), and `tests/scripts/distribution-presets.test.ts` which pins the named-preset contract. The author's intent ("deploy all games") is unchanged; only the mechanism name is corrected. See "OPEN QUESTION" in the comments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** The `deploy.yml` Build step selects the all-games preset (`GAMES_CONFIG=full`) so the production build includes all 8 games listed in `configs/full.json`.
- **AC2:** A local build with `GAMES_CONFIG=full` completes successfully (`npm run build` with the environment variable set).
- **AC3:** The resulting `dist/` contains the unified launcher with all 8 games plus the Gym selectable from the landing page.
- **AC4:** `RELEASE.md` describes the deploy build step consistently with the workflow (same-commit doc update, per the project doc-update policy for CI/CD changes).
- **AC5:** A regression test pins the deploy workflow's preset selection so it cannot silently revert to the `core-only` default (the defect this item fixes).

## Key Files

- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` — CI deployment workflow (one-line change)
- `configs/full.json` — already exists, lists all 8 games
- `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` — reads `GAMES_CONFIG` to discover games
- `RELEASE.md` — deploy workflow description (doc-update policy)
- `tests/scripts/deploy-workflow.test.ts` — new regression test (filename indicative)

## Outline

1. Add the regression test pinning the all-games preset on the deploy Build step (test-first; fails against the current workflow).
2. Set `GAMES_CONFIG=full` on the `deploy.yml` Build step.
3. Update `RELEASE.md` so its description of the deploy workflow matches.
4. Verify: `GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run build` exits 0 and `dist/`'s game selector catalogue contains all 8 games plus the Gym.

## Verification notes

- Deleting the `GAMES_CONFIG` assignment must fail the new regression test.
- `GAMES_CONFIG=all` must still hard-fail the build (proves the corrected preset name is the only working mechanism); no `configs/all.json` alias is to be created, since a duplicate preset would conflict with the preset contract pinned by CG-0MTRO77XA006YZZC.

# `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` is not self-contained: fails under a bare unit run

**discovered-from:CG-0MUIMM28K001W88F** (found while triaging the `npm --silent test` test-failure item)

## Problem statement

`tests/golf/replay.test.ts` invokes the replay CLI as a subprocess
(`node --import tsx/esm scripts/replay.ts`) and inherits the ambient
environment. The CLI registers replay adapters from the active preset
(`configs/<preset>.json`, selected by `GAMES_CONFIG`), and its default preset
is `core-only` — which contains no games, so no adapters are registered. The
golf adapter is only loaded when `GAMES_CONFIG` resolves to a preset that
includes golf (`solo`, `arcade`, `full`).

`scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` exports `GAMES_CONFIG="${GAMES_CONFIG:-full}"` before
its stages, so the test passes in the CI/full-suite path. Any *bare* targeted or
whole-profile unit run, however, uses the default `core-only` preset and the
file fails with four assertion failures:

```
Error: Could not auto-detect game type from transcript.
Available adapters: none. Use --game <type> to specify explicitly.
```

Failing assertions observed locally at `dev` HEAD `933644bc`
(`npx vitest run --project unit tests/golf/replay.test.ts`):
- `Tests  4 failed | 21 passed | 5 skipped (30)`
- `Test Files  1 failed | 2 passed (3)` when run alongside the two new main-street tests.

This contradicts the project's documented workflow, which tells developers and
agents to run the unit profile directly (`npx vitest run --project unit ...`,
`npm test -- --project unit`; see `AGENTS.md` → *Running Test Profiles* and
*When to run which tests*). A developer following that guidance sees a red unit
profile for reasons unrelated to their change, and a whole-profile
`npx vitest run --project unit` is currently red on a clean `dev` checkout.

Evidence (local, 2026-09-26):

| Command | `GAMES_CONFIG` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `npx vitest run --project unit tests/golf/replay.test.ts` | unset (→ `core-only`) | **4 failed**, 1 failed file; `Could not auto-detect game type ... Available adapters: none.` |
| `GAMES_CONFIG=full npx vitest run --project unit tests/golf/replay.test.ts` | `full` | 16 passed, 5 skipped |
| `GAMES_CONFIG=full npx tsx scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts --project unit` (whole profile) | `full` | 418 files passed, 7173 passed / 8 skipped — green |

The file's fixture path was also touched in the failing commit (`a341ec3c`,
"Incidental unblock: `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` fixture path corrected to the
launcher checkout layout"), so the fixture path itself is now correct and is
not the cause.

## Users

- **Developer / agent running the documented minimum test bar (primary):** needs
  `npx vitest run --project unit` to be green on a clean checkout without
  knowing which preset the target test implicitly depends on.
- **Maintainer (secondary):** needs tests to declare their own preconditions so
  preset/environment coupling is explicit rather than an ambient accident.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **The unit profile is green without environment priming:** `npx vitest run --project unit tests/golf/replay.test.ts` passes on a clean `dev` checkout with `GAMES_CONFIG` unset (and with `GAMES_CONFIG=core-only`). *Verified by:* the command exiting 0 and reporting no failed tests.
2. **The test declares its own preset:** the file arranges the preset it needs (e.g. sets `GAMES_CONFIG` explicitly in the subprocess environment for the adapter-dependent cases, or points `--game golf` at the adapter it requires) instead of relying on an ambient export from a shell wrapper. The chosen mechanism is documented in a code comment explaining why the CLI needs an adapter-registering preset.
3. **Adapter-dependent cases still exercise the real CLI path:** the tests that assert replay/validation behaviour against the golf fixture still run the real `scripts/replay.ts` subprocess with the golf adapter registered — they are not weakened into unit-level mocks or `it.skip`.
4. **No regression to the CI/full path:** `GAMES_CONFIG=full npx tsx scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts --project unit` remains green, and `tests/scripts/distribution-presets.test.ts` / `tests/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.test.ts` (which assert the `core-only` default and the shell runners' `GAMES_CONFIG=full` default) are unchanged or updated consistently.
5. **Sibling coupling audited:** any other test file with the same latent dependency on an ambient adapter-registering preset is identified and either fixed the same way or recorded. *Verified by:* grepping `tests/` for subprocess invocations of `scripts/replay.ts` (or other adapter-consuming CLIs) and confirming each sets its own preset.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments and the troubleshooting notes in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` if a new convention is introduced.
7. **Full project test suite passes with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken the tests to make them pass.** Skipping or mocking the adapter-dependent cases is not an acceptable fix; the run must remain a real CLI integration check.
- **Do not change the `core-only` default.** `core-only` is the deliberate production default (`GAMES_CONFIG` unset) and is asserted by existing tests; the fix belongs in the test, not the default preset.
- Keep changes surgical: this item covers test hermeticity only; the `[vitest-worker]` transient-contention failure is CG-0MUIMM28K001W88F.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` — the subprocess helper's environment (`runReplay`'s `env: { ...process.env }`) and the `FIXTURE_TRANSCRIPT` constant.
- `scripts/replay.ts` — adapter registration from the selected preset (`registerConfiguredAdapters(process.cwd())`).
- `scripts/adapters/index.ts` — `registerConfiguredAdapters` candidate-path resolution.
- `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` — `selectConfigPath` / `DEFAULT_PRESET = 'core-only'`.
- `configs/solo.json`, `configs/full.json` — presets that include golf.
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` — the `export GAMES_CONFIG="${GAMES_CONFIG:-full}"` that masks the defect in CI.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — CPU-contention / test-profile documentation to extend if a convention is introduced.

## Related work

- **CG-0MUIMM28K001W88F** — the `[test-failure]` item this was discovered from (transient Vitest worker RPC timeout defeating the retry guard).
- **CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0** — `validate all card text`; its commit `a341ec3c` carried the "incidental unblock" that corrected this file's fixture path and is the commit the reported failure was observed at.
- **CG-0MUILDS3200656TU** — referenced by that commit for the fixture-path correction.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: the fix hides a real preset-coupling bug (low).** The CLI's default preset is deliberately `core-only`; the test's need for an adapter is a *test* precondition, so setting it in the test is correct. *Mitigation:* AC2 requires a code comment stating why.
- **Risk: `GAMES_CONFIG` set per-subprocess diverges from the CI path (low).** *Mitigation:* AC4 requires the full-preset run to stay green.
- **Assumption:** the only preset-dependent surface in this file is the subprocess environment (the fixture path and the summary-report assertions are preset-independent).
- **Assumption:** other example-game replay tests, if any, are preset-independent or already covered by AC5's audit.

## Goal

Add the failing unit tests that pin the capacity-template contract (parent AC1–AC6) **before** the `HandView` fix lands, so the regression is captured as an executable specification.

## Context

Parent: CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ. Test-first item.

Today `HandView.computeCardPositions()` builds one row centred on the **current** `cards.length`, and `_computeOutlineSlots()` ghosts that row; adding a card therefore re-centres every card and every outline. The fix (sibling item) will derive positions from `maxSlots`. These tests must be red against the current code and green once the fix lands.

The existing Phaser mock in `tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts` (mock `scene.add.rectangle` / `image` / `text`) is the harness to reuse; assert on `scene._rectangles` (outlines), `handView` sprites, and `outlineRects`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC1: with `maxSlots` set, the set of outline slot positions for a given capacity is **identical** for a hand of 0, 1, … `maxSlots` cards (measured: the `outlineRects[i].x` for every `i` is unchanged across `setCards` of each size) — asserted as a unit test in `tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts`.
- Parent AC2: adding a card places it in the next empty slot to the right of the occupied run, and every already-placed card keeps its pre-add position (measured: for `addCard`, `sprite[i].x` before === after for all pre-existing `i`) — asserted for successive adds up to capacity and for successive `setCards` growth.
- Parent AC3: occupied outline slots still sit at the exact card position and rotation (`rect.x/y/rotation === sprite.x/y/rotation`), and extra capacity slots still render below every card — the CG-0MT6ER7YY003G680 invariant is preserved.
- Parent AC4: changing capacity (`setMaxSlots(n)`) re-lays the whole row and always yields exactly `n` slots; this is the only mutation that may move existing cards.
- Parent AC5: the empty-hand capacity row is unchanged from today's behaviour — `maxSlots` straight/arc slots centred on the hand centre — so an empty hand still shows the full capacity in the same place the cards will occupy.
- Parent AC6: unit tests verify AC 1–5, including a regression test that asserts positions do **not** move across successive `addCard`/`setCards` calls up to capacity, and that `setMaxSlots` does re-layout.
- Rotation/arc stability: per-card rotation and arc Y are derived from the capacity template, so they do not change when a card is added (assert `sprite.rotation` unchanged for pre-existing cards).
- `getInsertionPosition(i)` equals the rendered sprite position after inserting at `i` (guards the Main Street market→hand transfer).
- Over-capacity (transiently `cards.length > maxSlots`) is best-effort: the first `maxSlots` slots stay fixed, outlines stay capped at `maxSlots`, overflow cards continue to the right with the same step.
- Hands without `maxSlots` keep the existing centred-on-count layout (regression guard), and vertical cascade (already count-independent) is unchanged.
- Run via `npx vitest run --project unit tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts` (unit profile).

# Feature: Ship the ToneForge runtime synth module everywhere (commit it)

## Goal (user story)

As a player/tester running TCE in **any** environment — the launcher dev server,
a game-repo dev server, the built `dist/` (GitHub Pages), or the Electron
bundle — Main Street's ToneForge-backed synthesis audio works out of the box,
without anyone having to install the `tf` CLI or run `npm run tf:generate`
first.

## Context

Today the runtime synth module is generated on demand and never shipped:

- `scripts/tf-generate-synths.sh` writes `build/tf-synths/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs`
  (and a metadata module + WAVs + JSON) and **hard-fails** (`exit 1`) if the
  `tf` CLI is not on `PATH`.
- `build/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:15`) and Vite only copies `public/` into
  `dist/`, so the artefact is reachable on the dev server (which serves
  repo-root files) but **absent from `dist/` and the Electron bundle**.
- The runtime pre-checks `/build/tf-synths/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` and,
  when missing, logs `[MainStreet] ToneForge synth module not found …`
  (`src/tf/mainStreetTfModule.ts`).
- The decision recorded in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (§ToneForge Audio Generation) and
  `docs/the-build/audio.md` is explicitly **"we do not commit generated tf
  artifacts"** — this work item reverses that for the runtime module.
- CI never installs ToneForge, so generating at build time cannot work there.

The generated runtime module is **static JavaScript** (hard-coded Tone.js
factories) whose only runtime dependency is `tone`, which is already a shipped
dependency. It therefore does not need `tf`, WAVs, or network access at runtime.

## Proposed approach (confirm during planning)

1. Make the generated **runtime synth module** a source-controlled artefact so
   it is present in every checkout and copied into every build. Likely:
   generate/commit it at a path the runtime already serves
   (`public/build/tf-synths/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` in the launcher keeps
   the existing `/build/tf-synths/…` URL unchanged), or place it with the
   Main Street game assets and compose it via
   `repo-layout.json → gameAssets` (CG-0MUKYCG9L00587FA), updating the default
   URL.
2. Make `scripts/tf-generate-synths.sh` **fail-open**: a missing `tf` CLI is a
   warning/regeneration hint, never a build failure. `npm run build`/`dev` must
   not depend on `tf` and must not be changed to run generation.
3. Decide what is committed vs generated: commit the runtime module (and
   evaluate the metadata module); keep WAV/JSON generated output out of source
   control.
4. Update the docs to state which artefact is committed and how to regenerate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Clean checkout, no `tf`, no generation:** with the `tf` CLI absent and
   `npm run tf:generate` never run, `GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run dev` serves the
   runtime synth module at the exact URL `loadMainStreetTfModule()` requests,
   Main Street logs **no** `ToneForge synth module not found` warning, and
   synth-mapped SFX are active.
2. **Shipped build:** `GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run build` emits the module into
   `dist/` at the same URL path, and serving `dist/` (e.g. `npm run preview`)
   loads it with no warning. Same for `npm run build:electron`.
3. **Deterministic + single source of truth:** the committed module is the file
   the runtime loads; running `npm run tf:generate` (when `tf` is available)
   regenerates exactly that artefact with no drift, and the absence of `tf`
   never fails `npm run build` or `npm run dev`.
4. **Test coverage:** a unit test asserts the runtime default URL resolves to an
   on-disk artefact that is included in the public/build output, and that the
   module exports `TF_RUNTIME_MODULE`/`factories` including the expected keys
   (`card-draw`, `card-slide`, `card-place`, `card-discard`,
   `card-coin-collect`, `ui-notification-chime`, `card-table-ambience`,
   `construction-hammer`, `construction-saw`, `construction-lite-hammer`,
   `construction-lite-saw`, `crowd-cheer`).
5. **Docs:** `docs/DEVELOPER.md` §ToneForge Audio Generation and
   `docs/the-build/audio.md` no longer claim the runtime module is uncommitted;
   they state which artefact is source-controlled and how to regenerate it.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- Committing WAV or JSON generation output (binary/large) is out of scope.
- If the module must also be present in the **standalone `tce-main-street`
  repo**, that is a cross-repo follow-up; record it as a child/spin-off if the
  chosen placement does not cover it.

## Related

- Reverses the "do not commit generated tf artifacts" decision in
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` / `docs/the-build/audio.md`.
- Prior work: CG-0MOIY2VV200658OX (TF output spike + spec, open questions #2/#4),
  CG-0MOIY3MSR008EH0I (npm script + docs), CG-0MOIXHOWP003Y6E0 (runtime
  synthesis).
- Sibling asset composition: CG-0MUKYCG9L00587FA.
- Discovered-from: CG-0MUKYCG9L00587FA.

# Add per-turn running costs to Playground, Town Fountain and Community Shelter

## Summary

Give the three remaining free-to-run Main Street community-space cards a per-turn running cost, following the Park precedent (CG-0MU9NW9EP003B1AK) and the producer decision of 2026-09-29. Today the Playground (`cs-playground`), Town Fountain (`cs-fountain`) and Community Shelter (`cs-shelter`) have `ongoingCost` empty → 0, so they are free synergy/reputation anchors.

## Problem statement

The Park was given a 40 coins/turn running cost to stop costless synergy spam. Three other community spaces still have no ongoing cost, so the same "free anchor" dynamic remains for their synergies:

- **Playground** (`cs-playground`) — cost 400, Entertainment, +5 rep/turn, ongoing 0.
- **Town Fountain** (`cs-fountain`) — cost 500, Culture, +10 rep/turn, ongoing 0.
- **Community Shelter** (`cs-shelter`) — cost 600, Service, +15 rep/turn, ongoing 0 (retiered T6→T3, CG-0MT5VZJLS000B8KI).

## Users

- **Player** — building a Playground/Fountain/Shelter cluster should feel the per-turn drain as a real strategic cost.
- **Producer / balance owner** — wants a running-cost lever on every community space, not just Park/Library/Garden/Kiosk/Public Art.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Card data** — `cs-playground`, `cs-fountain` and `cs-shelter` in the Main Street `card-data.csv` each have a non-zero integer `ongoingCost`, confirmed with the producer before merge. **Proposed mapping (agent suggestion, producer-owned — confirm or override): Playground 20, Town Fountain 25, Community Shelter 30.**
2. **Descriptions** — each updated `card-data.csv` description states the running cost using the existing wording ("Costs N coins per turn to run."), consistent with Library/Community Garden/Park, and the `card-text-data-consistency` test passes.
3. **Deduction** — at end of turn each placed, unsold card deducts its `ongoingCost` through the existing `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()` path, clamped at 0 coins and logged with an insufficient-funds log when applicable.
4. **Tooltips** — each card's community-space tooltip shows `Ongoing cost: -N/turn`; each card's cash line shows `-N`.
5. **Sold-card exemption preserved** — a sold Playground/Fountain/Shelter incurs no ongoing cost (CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA).
6. **Tests** — add distinct coverage for each card's deduction, clamping and sold-exemption (no redundant duplicates); update any test that assumes these cards are free to run (e.g. `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` "does not deduct for zero-ongoing-cost cards" currently uses Playground + Fountain + Shelter and must be re-pointed at cards that remain free, or reworked).
7. **Balance sanity** — Monte Carlo and tutorial guardrails remain green; any drift is measured and reported, and no guardrail band is silently widened. Note the tutorial scenario places no Playground/Fountain/Shelter (verify).
8. **Docs** — update `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (Ongoing/turn column), `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`, `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` (special-cases) and any other doc listing these cards' running costs.
9. **Full project test suite passes.**

## Constraints

- **Integer economy (hard):** coins are whole integers (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6); no fractional `ongoingCost`.
- **Data is source of truth:** the running cost lives in `card-data.csv`; tooltip, overlay and deduction derive from it.
- **Charging semantics unchanged:** placed, unsold cards only; clamped at 0; reuse the existing community-space mechanism.
- **Balance values are producer-owned:** the proposed mapping is an agent suggestion; the producer confirms or overrides before merge.

## Existing state

- `cs-playground`: cost 400, baseIncome 0, Entertainment, rep 5, `ongoingCost` empty.
- `cs-fountain`: cost 500, baseIncome 0, Culture, rep 10, `ongoingCost` empty.
- `cs-shelter`: cost 600, baseIncome 0, Service, rep 15, `ongoingCost` empty.
- Park precedent: `docs/main-street/...`; commit `5ffd54a` in `tce-main-street` set `cs-park` to 40/turn and updated tests/tooltip/cash-line/docs.
- Test that assumes they are free: `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` "does not deduct for zero-ongoing-cost cards".

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` (tce-main-street repo) — set the three `ongoingCost` values and descriptions.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` — regenerated by the suite; no SVG face change expected (community-space ongoing cost is not baked in).
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` — add per-card deduction/clamp/sold coverage.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-tooltip.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/ongoing-cost-tooltips.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` — tooltip/cash-line coverage.
- `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` — rework the zero-cost test.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`, `card-catalog.md`, `balancing-methodology.md`.

## Related work

- **CG-0MU9NW9EP003B1AK** — Park running cost 40/turn (precedent; producer confirmed the integer-economy mapping).
- CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6 — integer economy ×100 rescale.
- CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA — sold cards excluded from ongoing costs.
- CG-0MRXYGM9B006I3PE — community-space ongoing-cost / Park-model synergy.
- CG-0MSQJ210I00491ZZ — Group B community-space expansion (added these three cards).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Value assumption:** the three proposed values (20/25/30) are an agent suggestion; the producer must confirm or override before merge.
- **Balance drift:** these cards appear in Monte Carlo simulations; run the guardrails and report drift rather than widening bands.
- **Test coupling:** the existing "does not deduct for zero-ongoing-cost cards" test uses exactly these three cards, so it must be updated (this is expected, not a regression).
